title: Empty WR-90 at 10 GHz: the largest field for 1 W and the power at which air breaks down
source: TE10 in an empty a × b guide carries P = ab|E0|²/(4Z_TE), Z_TE = η0 k0/β (D. M. Pozar, Microwave Engineering, 4th ed., Wiley 2012, §3.3, eq. 3.90), its field largest on the centre line, E0 = √(4Z_TE P/(ab)): for WR-90 at 10 GHz, Z_TE = 498.97 Ω, E0 = 2931.5 V/m at 1 W, and air (3 MV/m) breaks down at ab E_b²/(4Z_TE) = 1.0473 MW. Evaluated separately from EMCraft's code

quantities.quantity: largest field for 1 W at 10 GHz (V/m)
quantities.reason: the largest of the field sampled at every element's rule points and corners picks the interpolation's largest overshoot: +3 % with second-order elements of 3 mm (+1.8 % at the rule points alone, +0.8 % of those at 2 mm: it converges), on the safe side for breakdown
